I lived in China for ten years. Got married, and though it ended, I was blessed with a daughter who has spent her entire life growing up there. Its incredible watching her do her homework. The intricacy of the writing is astounding. Living in China is amazing, though maybe not for people who get anxious in crowds, as it often does feel overcrowded, especially if you try to visit well-known tourist attractions during public holidays. There's a LOT of people that want to look at the same thing you do. If you do want to visit China, i'd recommend practicing chopstick use, as you rarely find knives and forks in most restaurants
Don't believe all you hear about how bad life in China is, too, and dont judge the people on their governments actions...the same way you might not want to be judged on some of the things your government does

comments.text: A very interesting video about China. I was there in 2007, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2014, 2015, and 2024. It’s a beautiful country. I’m currently filming a documentary about Siberia and Russia.

replies.author: @jaseydalts
replies.text:
Did you revisit the same places on the different trips, or somewhere new each time? 
I lived in the same city, Jinan, from 2004 - 2010, then returned in 2018-2020 (until the pandemic started :O). The biggest noticeable difference, other than the upgrades in shopping malls, was how much less air pollution there was. It had sometimes been atrocious in my original trip, but the problem had obviously been seriously addressed in the interim period until my second stint. Oh, and the upgrade in train travel was also pretty astounding. Those intercity HSR trains felt like some of those old stories about how life in the 21st century was going to be were coming true
